suites.name: A. Agent contract: stdout, exit codes, error envelopes
suites.purpose: Everything an agent shells out to must return one parseable JSON document on stdout and a truthful exit code. This is the contract that breaks silently and breaks every integration at once.

scenarios.title: Effect CLI failures never put non-JSON on stdout
steps: Run `lucid bogus`, `echo '{}' | lucid plan ingest` (no --plan), and `lucid intent plan.html maybe`
Capture stdout and stderr separately for each
JSON.parse each stdout
scenarios.expected: Each exits 1 and stdout is empty or a single `{error:{code,message,detail}}` envelope. Today all three emit an Effect log block (`[23:39:36] ERROR (#17): Error: {"_tag":"CommandMismatch"...}`) on stdout, so every agent doing JSON.parse(stdout) throws instead of reading a typed error.
scenarios.testName: a refused command puts one JSON envelope on stdout
scenarios.mutation: src/cli/main.ts: neutralise the top-level catchAll that renders the error envelope, so an Effect failure prints its own diagnostics alongside the JSON and stdout stops being one document. Registered in test/e2e/regression/registry.ts, which notes the measured detail that removing the stderr LOGGER alone leaves it green - the catch is the fix.
scenarios.builtCapability: duplicated locally in two m2.x regression files

scenarios.title: A refusal always exits non-zero, including progress and context
steps: Run `lucid progress plan.html` (no flags) and `lucid progress plan.html --done -3`; echo $?
Run `lucid context plan.html --used 142000` (no --total); echo $?
Compare with `lucid ask plan.html` (no text)
scenarios.expected: All refusals exit 1 with an error envelope. Today progress and context print `{ok:false,error:...}` with exit 0, so `if lucid progress ...` in a shell treats a no-op as success.
scenarios.testName: context --used with no --total refuses in the same envelope as progress and ask
scenarios.mutation: src/core/context.ts: let the percentage derive from --used alone (`used !== undefined && total !== undefined && total > 0` -> `used !== undefined && (total ?? used) > 0` with the matching divisor) - context --used with no --total exits 0. Reds ONLY this test; the pre-existing refusal test stays green because used===undefined still refuses. The fixture creates the session directory BY HAND, and that is load-bearing: on a bare artifact the mutated build gets past validation and dies on ENOENT writing the sidecar - still exit 1, still an envelope - so the test would pass for a reason unrelated to its claim. Measured both ways.

scenarios.title: An unexpected runtime error is not emitted as an undocumented Lucid code

suites.name: K. Hub and process resilience
suites.purpose: Restarts, crashes, stale descriptors and multiple windows. This is where a wrong move corrupts the log with two appenders or kills every open tab.

scenarios.title: `open --restart` on a hub-hosted session leaves the hub and other tabs alive
steps: Start `lucid hub`, open two artifacts into it (two tabs in one window)
Run `lucid open <first> --restart`, check /hub/identity and both tabs
scenarios.expected: The hub process survives, both tabs keep working, and the second session is unaffected — stopServer refuses a descriptor carrying a `base`.
scenarios.testName: open --restart on a hub-hosted session leaves the hub and the other tab alive
scenarios.mutation: src/cli/self.ts: Invert `stopServer`'s hub-descriptor refusal so a descriptor carrying a `base` is signalled instead of left alone, and `open --restart` SIGTERMs the shared hub.

scenarios.title: `open --restart` replaces the running server without ending the session
steps: Open a session, annotate from the browser, rebuild the client bundle
Run `lucid open plan.html --restart`, reload the url, run `lucid wait --since <old cursor>`
scenarios.expected: A new server pid, NO session_ended event was written, and the earlier annotation is still delivered by wait. The bundle-freshness clause is deliberately dropped (D-078): the three claims above are what make a restart safe - a restart that writes session_ended silently ends a live review - and none of them needs the bundle-stamp capability to move, which is why that capability is not being built.
scenarios.testName: open --restart replaces the server pid without ending the session
scenarios.mutation: src/cli/run.ts: make --restart end the session instead of stopping the server (`if (options.restart) await stopServer(paths)` -> `await deliver(paths, { t: "session_ended" })`) - the log gains a session_ended and the test reds on the event list. Wrong-reason guards: server.json pids compared before/after (a reattach would make everything else trivially true), session_ended absence read from the log directly, the annotation written before anything is killed so its delivery is a real round trip through the replaced process. Bundle freshness deliberately not asserted (D-078).

scenarios.title: A hub that dies between accept and handshake fails loudly, never split-brains

Inspect the exit code and whether a dedicated server was spawned
scenarios.expected: Exit 1 with SERVER_ERROR "the hub accepted the session but its mount never answered"; no dedicated per-session server behind the hub's mount (two appenders would corrupt the log).
scenarios.testName: a hub that accepts a session and never serves it fails loudly, never split-brains
scenarios.mutation: src/cli/run.ts: neutralise the post-accept handshake guard (`if (!identity)` -> `if (false)`) - open silently serves a session the hub already owns, putting two appenders on one log (measured red against a stub hub that accepts and never serves; killing a real hub BEFORE open does not enter this branch and left the guard unproven)

scenarios.expected: The handshake rejects the impostor (session path mismatch), the stale descriptor is removed, a fresh server is spawned, and the printed url points at the new port.
scenarios.testName: a stale viewer never posts its message into whichever session took its port

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous opens of one artifact yield one session and one server

scenarios.blockedBy: Findings #54 and #55: two concurrent opens append two session_opened events (check-then-act, not guarded by appendEventsIf) and the loser orphans a __serve that `end` cannot reap and the listing cannot see. The row's true half - one url, one server - is already covered; asserting only that would answer the easy clause and leave the two-appenders state unmentioned. Returns when both are fixed.

scenarios.title: A restarted hub on the same port re-adopts open windows without a reload
steps: Start the hub, open two sessions, load the shell (drafts typed)

suites.name: M. Launcher and forks

newCapabilities: raw-cli: a runner that returns {stdout, stderr, code} without JSON.parse. makeCli.run today parses stdout and execFileAsync throws on non-zero exit, so no existing test can even observe a polluted stdout or a wrong exit code — the single highest-value harness gap.

durable-path-fixture: a fixture rooted outside $TMPDIR, and a runner that omits LUCID_ALLOW_TEMP. Every e2e today sets LUCID_ALLOW_TEMP=1 in a temp dir, so the entire volatile-path refusal path is structurally untestable.

kill-server: read server.json for the pid and SIGKILL/SIGTERM the dedicated session server (and the hub) mid-test. Today only `lucid end` is used, which is a clean shutdown and exercises none of the suspended/stale-descriptor paths.

fixed-port-hub-restart: start a hub on a stable port, stop it, and start a second one on the same port with the same registry inside one test. startHub uses --port 0 and its stop() deletes the state dir, so reattach and self-recovery cannot be exercised.
multi-window: two browser contexts against one hub, with helpers to assert broadcast, independent close and independent scope. No test opens a second context today.

route-intercept: page.route helpers for delay / abort / status+body stubbing of /__lucid/message, /annotation, /asset, /fork and /hub/events. No e2e uses page.route at all, so every slow-send, partial-failure, 409 and server-reason path is unreachable.

hit-test: a reusable elementFromPoint assertion ("this control is what a real pointer would hit"). Exists as one ad-hoc block in shell.e2e.ts; needs generalizing to cover tooltips, the drawer overlay and picker rows.

scale-fixture: generate N artifacts/sessions (12, 20, 60) in one or several projects cheaply. Required for strip scrolling, the 10-stream cap, the port pool, the 60-row picker and the large-tree status timing.

concurrent-cli: fire several CLI invocations simultaneously (or hold a long-running one) and compare their payloads and the log. Needed for two waits, two opens, mid-flight restart, and the ask/reply/progress/viewer write race.
compiled-binary: `bun run build` then drive dist/lucid in e2e. Every test runs `bun run src/cli/main.ts`, so selfInvocation regressions in the shipped binary ship green.
clipboard: grant clipboard-read/write permissions on the context and read navigator.clipboard, plus a stub that rejects writeText.
stub-harness-launcher: run `lucid launch` as a long-lived child with a stub harness recipe (test/launch-stub.ts exists but is not driven end to end), capture its substituted argv, and send it SIGINT.
log-corruption: mutate log.ndjson mid-test — append a torn tail, replace a committed line — and assert the recovery path.
bundle-stamp: touch or rebuild the chrome bundle mid-test so the dev stamp moves, for --restart-serves-new-bundle and the self-reload.
no-network: run a full loop with outbound networking disabled, to prove the loopback-only claim.
